title: Let a human name the reattribution for a record whose text makes no claim
action: Extend bee decisions reattribute with an explicit pair: --id <decision id> --to <feature slug> (decision-attribution D5 residual, filed P3). Semantics: both flags together or neither (the bare verb stays the automatic text-claim pass). With the pair: refuse when the id names no decision; refuse a blank --to; refuse when the record's own text opens with a <slug> D<n> claim naming a DIFFERENT feature than --to (the manual door never contradicts the record's own text - that is the automatic pass's territory); when the stamp already equals --to report zero changed (idempotent); otherwise rewrite ONLY the feature field of exactly that record under the decisions lock, carrying every other line through byte-for-byte, and report old -> new. Declare the two flags on the registry entry (edit as DATA, round-trip serialization check). Update the registry description's one-time wording to note the targeted pair. Tests: pair corrects an unclaiming record; refusal on a contradicting text claim; refusal on unknown id; blank --to refuses; second run reports zero; only feature differs on the corrected line. Then run it for real for the five prompt-work-record records (f9bf6456, 34944b7a, 5944ebbb, 856789db, bd78f64a -> prompt-work-record) and quote the counts in the cap.

truths: --id/--to corrects a record whose text makes no claim, feature being the only field that differs
a record whose text claims a different feature refuses with a teach line naming the automatic pass
unknown id and blank --to refuse; a stamp already equal to --to reports zero
the flags are served and declared; registry_dispatch stays green both directions
the five prompt-work-record records carry feature prompt-work-record afterwards and a re-run reports zero
